rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2.1 <U+2013> two lysimeter experiments (clayey Vertisol and sandy soil) with lettuce under DI/SDI with and without nanobubble-oxygenated TWW, 4<U+2013>5 replicates per treatment. Q2: Section 3.1 and Table 3 <U+2013> average soil air O2 concentration at 10 cm significantly increased under both DI and SDI with ONB-TWW in both soils (p<0.03); Discussion states ONB irrigation raised soil air O2 regardless of soil type and drip method. Q4: Section 3.1 <U+2013> the authors measured dissolved O2 added by ONB (+14 mg/L, ~20 mg O2 per litre), measured WFPS via TDR, and built an O2 mass balance against measured CO2 fluxes (~1% of daily O2 consumption), i.e. the intermediate pathway from oxygenated water to soil aeration was quantified. Q8: Section 2.3 <U+2013> in the clayey-soil experiment the continuous O2 sensors were flooded and could not give accurate readings; Discussion <U+2013> the authors state it is hard to explain from the mass balance how such small O2 additions raised soil air O2, and that mechanisms remain unresolved.
rows.notes: The study supports only the 'increasing soil aeration' part of the passage; it does not measure soil mechanical strength, air permeability or air-filled porosity. Q3: soil O2 was measured by two instruments (perforated-bottle sampling with an O2 meter and KE-50 sensors), but both measure the same quantity at the same depth and the sensors failed in clay, so treated as one method; the CO2-based mass balance is a mechanism check rather than independent confirmation of the aeration result. Q5: only two soils and one crop. Q6: lysimeter pots only. Q7: effect reported regardless of soil type; no condition stated as a requirement. Q9: Table 3 reports soil air O2 means without SE, and the statistics section's 'means <U+00B1> SE' is only shown for physiological parameters (Table 4), not for the aeration result; supplementary Fig SI-2 not available.

notes: Full text available; supplementary figures (SI-1 to SI-3) referenced but not included.
